From the judge's explanation

Both parties are looking at the same record, so here is what it shows.

The driver did arrive and wait. The trip record logs the 'I'm Here' tap at 19:24:52, the GPS trace shows an unbroken hold inside the pickup geofence of 471 seconds across 47 qualifying fixes (19:24:52 to 19:32:43), and the trip was cancelled at 19:32:46 under RIDER_NO_SHOW. Standing alone, the four limbs of POL-NS-01 are met, and the driver's statement that he waited the full time is true as far as the dwell goes.

How to appeal: Either party may appeal once within 30 days. A different human reviewer hears it, and only record evidence may be added.

POL-GEN-05: the monetary effect is SGD 4.50 against an execution threshold of SGD 8.00. It does not exceed the threshold, so the amount is executed automatically on issue, subject to POL-GEN-04.

Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

Each draft's own explanation

Both parties are looking at the same record, so here is what it shows. The driver did arrive and wait. The trip record logs the 'I'm Here' tap at 19:24:52, the GPS trace shows an unbroken hold inside the pickup geofence of 471 seconds across 47 qualifying fixes (19:24:52 to 19:32:43), and the trip was cancelled at 19:32:46 under RIDER_NO_SHOW. Standing alone, the four limbs of POL-NS-01 are met, and the driver's statement that he waited the full time is true as far as the dwell goes. But POL-NS-01 makes the fee chargeable only where no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, and POL-NS-04 displaces it here. All three of its limbs hold. (a) The chat log shows the rider sent two coordinating messages inside the waiting window — 'im at the pickup, which car are you? i cant see you' at 19:25:22 and 'hello? are you here' at 19:27:22. Each is a request for the driver's position and a statement that the rider cannot see the vehicle, which is exactly the content limb (a) names. (b) The driver neither replied nor called: the chat log contains no driver message and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty. (c) The rider's own track places the device within 12.1 m of the pin on all 85 qualifying fixes across the window, far inside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider-presence radius.
